justification: GST-1821 (an outside review reads clean only from a last-line VERDICT token): preregistered no-loss probe, gpt-6-astra at high effort, codex-cli 0.167.0, six seeded-bug repos and three clean repos, two trials per case and arm, 54 scored runs. Codex's structured step moved from `codex review --base` (arm R) to `codex exec` with gstack's prompt, [P0]-[P3] tags and the last-line VERDICT request (arm X). X caught the seeded bug in 12 of 12 bug runs, R in 12 of 12 and the no-gstack arm in 12 of 12, so no catch was lost; all three arms are saturated, so a loss on subtler bugs is not ruled out. X ended with the VERDICT line in 18 of 18 runs and read clean on all 6 clean-case runs. The adversarial outside brief and the other outside prompt-file lines change only their closing request (the Recommendation line is kept and the same VERDICT request is appended); their finding, severity and Blocks instructions are byte-identical and were not probed separately. Free replay of 681 captured outside replies through the new parser: 0 moved toward clean. Fix round (Captain grant a-aec3882c9d48): Codex's structured step now appends the base-branch diff to its prompt (the same REPOSITORY CONTEXT block the Claude path uses, header and diff in one guarded write), puts the filesystem boundary first in its request line, and drops two lead sentences; the parser reads the verdict from the raw last line, so inline code after the token no longer reads clean, and reads VERDICT: CLEAN beside unlabeled numbered items as unverified. Rerun at the fix-round tree, no paid run: the free replay's 681 inputs keep identical transition counts (0 toward clean) and all 54 scored probe replies keep their verdicts (0 changed; caught 12/12 in every arm; 18/18 verdict lines).
